purpose: Penicillin V is an antibiotic used to treat common bacterial infections such as strep throat, ear infections, and skin infections. It can also be used to prevent infections in people with certain heart conditions or weakened immune systems. It only works against bacteria — it will not help with viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_it_works: Penicillin V works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of that wall like a protective shield — penicillin pokes holes in it and breaks it down. Without that protective wall, the bacteria cannot survive and eventually die off, helping your body clear the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and stomach upset. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop hives, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or have trouble breathing, as this could be a serious allergic reaction. Always let your healthcare provider know if you have had a penicillin or any antibiotic allergy before. Make sure to finish the entire course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better — stopping early can allow the infection to come back or become resistant to treatment.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth every 6 to 8 hours, depending on the type and severity of the infection. It is often taken for 7 to 10 days. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help prevent stomach upset. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your prescription.
